calls.prompt:
Edit the first picture, a rough 3D render, into ONE finished building sprite for a pastoral isometric railway game: the Big Farm Halt, a timber grain barn with a loading dock and a round silo, the SAME building as in the third picture, in the view named under View. Paint over the first picture: its shape, outline, camera and layout stay exactly as they are (every roof, wall, chimney, opening and part where the render has it, nothing added outside its outline or taken out of it), but EVERY surface is painted again in the game's painted style, that of the second picture, the style board: crisp pixel-art-inspired clustered shading, broad readable masses, three or four shades per material, restrained detail, a strong silhouette. The render's surfaces are soft, smeared and patchy, and the walls that the front view never showed were invented by the 3D reconstruction (they are named under View). Paint all of them anew: where the third picture shows a surface, take its stones, bricks, planks, doors, windows and fittings from it, crisp; where the render has invented a surface, paint it as this same building would have it, plausibly and in the same style, from the materials and details of the sides that are known, and never leave it soft, blurred, smeared or plain. The palette family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B, slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest, lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest (the render's light was corrected for the turn; the painting follows the game's light). Nothing at or above cursor white #ECE4D0 and nothing as strong as selection amber #E8AA48.

Camera: keep the render's camera exactly: orthographic 2:1 isometric, 30 degrees down, ground edges two pixels across for each pixel down, vertical edges vertical, no perspective. Do not rotate, tilt, turn, resize, shift or reshape the building: its silhouette stays where the render's is, and the picture is checked against it. Show the whole building with a clear margin all round, as the render does.

Ground: paint only the building. No plinth, ground, floor slab, grass, shadow or pad under it that the render does not have; keep the foot of the two visible walls plain and straight where the render has it, with no bushes, crates, steps or loose objects added in front of it.

View. The building is turned half round. The front faces the upper right, away from the camera, and nothing of it is in this picture: no entrance door and none of the front's windows or other features on either visible wall. The lower-left wall is the BACK, plainer than the front; the lower-right wall is the left-hand side. The lower-left wall is the BACK, the same wall as the lower-right wall of the r1 picture: a plain timber gable end under the slate roof with a small window high in the gable, and no loading dock, no crates and no ramp. The lower-right wall is the left-hand side, the same wall as the lower-left wall of the r3 picture: the long timber wall, plainer than the right-hand one: vertical planks on the same stone base course, two small windows and timber braces, no door and no silo. Where r1 or r3 is not attached, take that wall from these words. The roof is r0's: dark slate, its ridge along the long walls, the small louvred dormer on one slope and the cream-stone chimney with its copper pot at the same places; the silo stands at the end of the long wall where r0 has it and turns with the building.

Invented in the first picture (the front view never showed it): both walls (the barn's plain timber with two windows, the silo seen from the other side). Paint these surfaces anew, crisp and plausible, in this building's own materials and details; the first picture's soft or smeared look is not kept.

References: the first is the scaffold's lit render, the picture to paint over; the second is the style board. The third is this building as it is in the game today, seen from the front (view r0): take its materials, details and character from it and paint them over the first picture, surface by surface; the shape, the angle, the outline and the layout are the first picture's and do not change, and the third picture's angle, footprint and any dark glow round it are not used. Paint the SAME building at the size the first picture has it: it is not a mirror image and not a copy of the third picture, and do not paint the third picture again. There, in view r0, the lower-left wall is the front: the short gable end with the loading dock, the crates and the sacks. In this picture the front faces away, hidden behind the building: neither visible wall is the front, and what the front has does not show on them. The fourth reference is this same building in view r1 (the kept picture): its lower-right wall is the BACK, and that wall is the lower-left wall of this picture. The fifth is this same building in view r3 (the kept picture): its lower-left wall is the left-hand side, and that wall is the lower-right wall of this picture. Copy both walls as they stand in those references: the same height, shape under the roof, windows and doors, painted in the same way. Where r1 or r3 is not attached, take that wall from the words above.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building surfaces. Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow, or loose objects standing apart from the building.

Output size: 1024 x 1024.

Correction: your last r2 again exceeded the boundary limit (36.35 canvas px, maximum 24; best-fit IoU 0.9635). The chimney and roof at its left end, the silo's cone and pipe and the small loading-canopy projection must keep the exact outlines of the first image. Do not invent a more regular shape for these parts or move the corner posts: paint the original geometry in place, with its precise outline unchanged.
